metadata.title: Interfaces or Bodies? A 24-Instance Pilot Measurement of ε-Sufficient Context for Language-Model Code Editing in Go
metadata.description: A recent note defines a context as ε-sufficient for a code-editing language model when the model's pass rate on it is within ε of its pass rate on the best context in a stated family, and proves that under a bounded reader this property is not closed under superset. This report gives the first measurements. From 282 trunk commits of the GitHub CLI (June--October 2026) screened by fixed, logged rules, 24 fail-to-pass instances were obtained. Holding localisation at the gold write-set, three models edited each instance under up to nine contexts: task text only; the write-set alone; the write-set plus the exported interfaces of its direct dependencies (A1); the same with full bodies (A1b); A1 plus the interfaces of dependent packages (A1F); and A1 padded with unrelated same-repository code to 32k, 64k, 128k and 200k prompt tokens. Patches were verified by hidden fail-to-pass tests and by the tests of the write-set and its dependents. On Claude Haiku 5.5 (10 samples per cell) interfaces outperformed bodies by +0.04 [+0.01, +0.08] at one third of the tokens, outperformed the write-set alone by +0.07 [+0.02, +0.13], and adding dependent-package interfaces did not help (-0.05). Padding to 200k tokens changed the pass rate by +0.03 [-0.09, +0.15] on Haiku, -0.04 [-0.33, +0.22] on Claude Sonnet 5.5 (3 samples per cell) and -0.07 [-0.19, 0.00] on Claude Opus 5 (3 samples per cell, the 10 instances Sonnet could not solve from task text alone): the two stronger models show a small negative sign whose interval reaches zero, and the degradation curve is flat within the resolution of this pilot. Sonnet solved 14 of 24 instances at least once from the task text alone, Haiku 4 of 24, which makes a task-only control essential for any confirmatory study. Run-to-run variation at default sampling was substantial (25% of Haiku cells non-unanimous). The whole measurement cost about 61 in API calls. Instances, contexts, harness and all 2,363 verdicts are released. This is an exploratory pilot on one repository; it fixes the design of a preregistered study and makes no confirmatory claim.
metadata.notes: Exploratory pilot on one repository and three models of one vendor; it fixes the design of a preregistered study and makes no confirmatory claim. The data zip includes instances, the mining log, the harness and all verdict records.
